When a Lambda function is executed, it is allocated a certain amount of memory, and the function must complete its execution within that memory limit. If the function exceeds its memory limit, it will be terminated and an error will be returned.

In general, the more memory a Lambda function uses, the slower it will perform. This is because the function will have to spend more time allocating and deallocating memory, which can slow down the execution of the function. Additionally, if the function uses too much memory, it may cause the Lambda service to run out of memory, which can cause other functions to be terminated.

To optimize the performance of a Lambda function written in Node.js, it is important to keep the memory usage as low as possible while still meeting the requirements of the function. This can be achieved by using efficient algorithms, minimizing the use of global variables, and avoiding the use of unnecessary libraries or modules.

It is also important to note that the amount of memory allocated to a Lambda function can affect its cost. The more memory a function uses, the higher its cost will be. Therefore, it is important to strike a balance between the performance requirements of the function and the cost of running it.<|eot_id|>

The issue is that the Python code is not passing the login credentials to the Power BI website. To fix this, you can use the `requests` library to send a POST request to the Power BI login page with your credentials, and then use the resulting session to download the PDF.

Here's an updated version of your code that should work:
```python
import requests
import os

# Power BI login URL
login_url = "https://app.powerbi.com/PowerBI.WebApi/Account/Login"

# Power BI report URL
full_url = "https://app.powerbi.com/groups/me/rdlreports/1bdef01c-30a3-4150-aff2-b3ec4c9edf86?rp:AdviceDeathScriptMERGEDMonthStartDate=6/1/2023&rp:AdviceDeathScriptMERGEDIncomingcall=Aria%20Park&rdl:format=PDF"

# Power BI login credentials
username = "your_username"
password = "your_password"

# Send a POST request to the Power BI login page with the credentials
response = requests.post(login_url, data={
    "username": username,
    "password": password
})

# Check if the login was successful
if response.status_code == 200:
    # If successful, use the resulting session to download the PDF
    response = requests.get(full_url, cookies=response.cookies)
    filename = f"AriaPark.pdf"
    with open(filename, 'wb') as file:
        file.write(response.content)
    print("Reports have been successfully downloaded.")
else:
    print("Login failed. Please check your credentials.")
```
Replace `your_username` and `your_password` with your actual Power BI login credentials. This code should now download the PDF without any issues.<|eot_id|>
